guides.definition: Creates an Express application with one GET route and starts listening. Requires Express in the active Node.js project; Hypershell does not install it.

examples.title: Expose a health endpoint
examples.explanation: The route handler serializes the value as JSON; production servers should also define centralized error and shutdown behavior.

guides.definition: Enables JSON body parsing and validates a required request field. Requires Express in the active Node.js project; Hypershell does not install it.

parameters.name: fieldName
parameters.description: Body property required by the endpoint.

examples.title: Create a named item
examples.explanation: express.json parses matching request bodies before the route; explicit validation avoids treating malformed input as domain data.

guides.definition: Adds the four-argument Express error handler after application routes. Requires Express in the active Node.js project; Hypershell does not install it.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: HTTP status returned for unhandled errors.

examples.title: Return an internal-server response
examples.explanation: Express recognizes error middleware by its four parameters; delegating after headers were sent lets the default handler close the response correctly.
